historical_anchors.US_official: US Army official history places 80-100 Japanese tanks in the Lingayen force.
historical_anchors.regimental_OOB: 7th Tank Regiment: 34 Type89 + 14 Type95 (plus a very small Type97 reinforcement later); 4th Tank Regiment about 38 Type95.
historical_anchors.US_tanks: 108 M3 Stuarts initially in 192nd/194th Tank Battalions.
historical_anchors.captured_by_20_Feb: 14th Army reported 31 captured tanks by 20 Feb 1942.
historical_anchors.Baliuag: US claimed 8 Japanese tanks; Japanese record cited in secondary reconstruction admits 1 destroyed and 1 damaged.
historical_anchors.late_Bataan: 7th Tank Regiment commander was killed 6 Apr during an attack in which US 37mm AT guns engaged a six-tank group.
historical_anchors.Shinhoto: Two Shinhoto are a hard historical Corregidor-era combat anchor.

branch_vehicle_mix.reason: Branch prewar retrofit pool and faster acceptance permit a slightly larger urgent reinforcement, but shipping/training keeps it platoon-sized.

first_pass_outcome.US_final_national_tank_loss_delta: approximately 0; the force is ultimately destroyed/captured anyway

captured_vehicle_effect.note: Not all captured tanks are immediately serviceable or retained. Some can follow the 4th Tank Regiment/16th Army; others remain depot/training assets.
captured_vehicle_effect.guard: Captured Allied tanks are a separate pool and do not become Japanese-produced hulls.

time_effect.Bataan_final_assault: 0-12 hours earlier/less costly centered after the late Shinhoto reinforcement and better Japanese readiness

post_campaign_allocation.4th_Tank_Regiment: Moves to 16th Army/NEI; do not leave its survivors in Philippine reserve.
post_campaign_allocation.7th_Tank_Regiment: Remains until May then is reassigned toward Kwantung Army; not free until transport is completed.
